plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Increase QQQI to 25% to favor income and broad index exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5%/month return. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Increase QQQI to 20% to balance income with growth.
Trim CRWD to 15% to reduce single name concentration.
Buy DDOG at 5% as a strong new scanner setup to add quality tech exposure.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index, quality tech, and a small amount of leveraged exposure. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged exposure in uptrends.
Add to CRWD to 20% to press a strong performing asset.
Buy DDOG at 8% and SMCI at 5% to add high-scoring scanner setups.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4%/month by leveraging strong uptrends and high-scoring setups. It uses and adds to leveraged ETFs, which can amplify both gains and losses. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Increase QQQI to 40% to prioritize income and low drawdown.
Trim QQQ to 10% to shift focus towards income-generating assets.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable monthly distributions over growth. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market selloffs; this is not a savings account.
